1.note: The phrase “in his … place” is a metaphor meaning “instead of him.” Alternate translation: [instead of his father]

3.q: The king of Egypt removed him at Jerusalem
3.note: The idiom “removed him at Jerusalem” means that he caused him no longer to be king in Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [The king of Egypt removed him from being king in Jerusalem]
Here the word “land” represents the people who lived there. Alternate translation: [fined the people of the land]

3.q: one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold
3.note: You may convert this to a modern measure. A talent was about 33 kilograms. Alternate translation: [thirty-three hundred kilograms of silver and thirty-three kilograms of gold] or [about 3,300 kilograms of silver and 33 kilograms of gold] (See also: [Numbers](ta:translate-numbers))

4.note: These are the names of men.

5.q: what was evil in the sight of Yahweh his God
5.note: Here “sight” represents judgment. Yahweh saw and did not approve of Jehoiakim’s actions. Alternate translation: [what Yahweh judged to be evil] or [what Yahweh considered to be evil]

6.note: The word “him” refers to Jehoiakim. Jehoiakim represents either Jerusalem or the nation of Judah. Alternate translation: [attacked Jerusalem] or [attacked Judah]

7.note: Since Nebuchadnezzar was king, he may have had his soldiers do this. Alternate translation: [Nebuchadnezzar also had his soldiers carry]
Here the word “house” represents the temple. Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh]

8.q: the disgusting things that he did
8.note: This usually refers to worshiping false gods, which Yahweh hated.

This idiom refers to things that he did for which people could accuse him of wrong. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [what people found against him] or [things that he did for which people could accuse him] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))
Alternate translation: [anyone can look in the book … Israel and see they are written there]

8.q: they are written in the book
8.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [someone has written them in the book] or [you can read of them in the book]

8.q: the book of the kings of Judah and Israel
8.note: This is a book that no longer exists. See how you translated this in 2 Chronicles 35:27.
The phrase “in his place” is a metaphor meaning “instead of him.” Alternate translation: [became king instead of Jehoiakim]

9.q: eight years old … three months and ten days
what was evil in the sight of Yahweh
9.note: Here “sight” here represents judgment. Yahweh saw and did not approve of Jehoiachin’s actions. Alternate translation: [what Yahweh judged to be evil] or [what Yahweh considered to be evil]

10.note: Here “house” represents the temple. Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh]

12.q: what was evil in the sight of Yahweh his God
12.note: Here “sight” represents judgment. Yahweh saw and did not approve of Zedekiah’s actions. Alternate translation: [what Yahweh his God judged to be evil] or [what Yahweh his God considered to be evil]

12.q: who spoke from the mouth of Yahweh
12.note: Here the word “mouth” represents the words that Yahweh spoke. Alternate translation: [who spoke the words that Yahweh spoke to him]

13.q: Zedekiah stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning to Yahweh
13.note: The phrases “stiffened his neck” and “hardened his heart” are both metaphors that mean to become stubborn. Zedekiah refusing to worship Yahweh is spoken of as if he refused to turn to Yahweh. Alternate translation: [Zedekiah stubbornly refused to worship Yahweh] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

14.q: they followed the disgusting practices of the nations
14.note: The idiom “followed the … practices” means to do those things. Alternate translation: [they did the disgusting things that the nations did]
This phrase refers to worshiping other gods.

14.q: They polluted the house of Yahweh
14.note: A place that is unfit to be used for God’s purposes is spoken of as if it were physically dirty. The word “house” represents the temple. Alternate translation: [They polluted the temple of Yahweh] (See also: [Metonymy](ta:figs-metonymy))

16.q: the wrath of Yahweh arose against his people
16.note: Here the word “arose” refers to beginning an action. Yahweh punishing his people in his anger is spoken of as if his wrath were a person who acted against them. Alternate translation: [in his wrath, Yahweh began to punish his people]

16.q: there was no help for it
16.note: This idiom means that nobody could do anything to prevent what happened. Alternate translation: [there was no way to avoid it]

17.q: God brought on them the king of the Chaldeans, who
17.note: The idiom “brought on them” means to cause to attack with his army. Alternate translation: [God caused the king of the Chaldeans to attack them, and he]

17.q: who killed their young men with the sword
17.note: The king probably did not personally kill their young men. Rather, his army killed them. Alternate translation: [whose army killed their young men with swords]

17.q: God gave them all into his hand
17.note: Here “hand” is a metonym for the power to defeat them. Alternate translation: [God allowed the Chaldean army to defeat them]

18.q: the house of God … the house of Yahweh
18.note: The word “house” represents the temple. Alternate translation: [the temple of God … the temple of Yahweh]

20.q: The king carried away to Babylon
20.note: Here “the king” refers to his soldiers whom he ordered to do the work. The phrase “carried away” is an idiom that means to forcefully bring them to Babylon. Alternate translation: [The king had his army forcefully take to Babylon] (See also: [Idiom](ta:figs-idiom))

20.q: until the rule of the kingdom of Persia
20.note: Alternate translation: [until the kingdom of Persia came to power]

21.q: the word of Yahweh by the mouth of Jeremiah
21.note: Here the noun “word” can be translated with the verb “spoke.” The word “mouth” represents Jeremiah. Alternate translation: [what Yahweh spoke through Jeremiah] or [the word from Yahweh that Jeremiah spoke]

21.q: until the land should have enjoyed its Sabbath rests
21.note: The people were supposed to obey the Sabbath law by not farming the land every seventh year. This phrase speaks about this as if the land were a person that would obey the Sabbath law and rest. Alternate translation: [until the land had rested according to the Sabbath law] or [until, as required by the Sabbath law, no one had farmed the land]

21.q: It observed its Sabbath for as long as it lay abandoned
21.note: The word “it” refers to the land. The land is spoken of as if it were a person who observed the Sabbath. Alternate translation: [The requirements of the Sabbath law were fulfilled as long as the land lay abandoned]

21.q: in order to pass seventy years in this way
21.note: “so that 70 years passed while the land lay abandoned”

22.note: This refers to the beginning of the reign of King Cyrus.

22.q: so that the word of Yahweh by the mouth of Jeremiah might be carried out
22.note: Here the noun “word” can be translated with the verb “spoke.” The word “mouth” represents Jeremiah. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [so that what Yahweh spoke through Jeremiah might happen] or [so that the word from Yahweh that Jeremiah spoke might happen] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

22.q: Yahweh motivated the spirit of Cyrus, king of Persia
22.note: Motivating the spirit is a synecdoche for making someone want to act. Alternate translation: [Yahweh made Cyrus, king of Persia, want to act]

23.q: all the kingdoms of the earth
23.note: This is an exaggeration, as there were kingdoms over which Cyrus did not rule.

23.q: to build a house for him
23.note: Here the word “house” represents a temple. Alternate translation: [to build a temple for him]

23.q: Let him go up to the land
23.note: Alternate translation: [Let that person go up to the land of Judah]
